info.title: LiMDM admin API
info.description: REST API of the LiMDM console. Every action runs through the same functions as the console, with the same role rules, validation and audit entries. Authenticate with an API token from the console (Administration, API tokens) as a bearer token. The console app (/app/) uses the session cookie instead: every request must come from the console origin (Origin, Sec-Fetch-Site) and every state change must carry the CSRF token of GET /api/v1/me in the X-CSRF-Token header. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details. Lists are paged with limit and an opaque cursor. Each token may send 600 requests per minute; failed authentications are limited to 20 per client address in five minutes. Tenants: a token created in a tenant (multi tenancy, see docs/tenants.md) sees and changes only that tenant's devices, commands, library items, blueprints, tags and audit entries; shared library items and blueprints of the Default tenant are readable but not writable, and objects of other tenants answer 404. Global tokens see every tenant. Metrics need a global token. List conventions (devices is the reference): filter takes the query language (free words, key:value, key:"quoted value", every term must match), sort takes a field with - for descending, cursor continues a page from next_cursor, and <list>/facets answers counts per value for the same filter.

parameters.description: Query language: free words match host name, OS, id, blueprint or tags; keys status (compliant, in-grace, non-compliant, stale, pending, retired), os, tag, blueprint, agent, check (failing check id), pkg (name with optional version comparison), app, flatpak, remote, seen (>7d older, <2h newer; m, h, d). Example: status:non-compliant os:"Ubuntu 24" tag:prod. Unknown keys are an error.

post.description: Same commands and rules as the console: scripts, lost mode, wipe, allow_uninstall, user, software and app commands need the admin role; lost and wipe need confirm set to the host name. Audited as command.<type>. Roles admin and helpdesk, not read only. With four eyes approval on (wipe, lost mode, scripts) nothing is queued: the answer is 202 with the approval_id of a pending request that another admin decides in the console or through /api/v1/approvals/{id}.

202.description: Queued (a Command), or, when the command needs four eyes approval, an approval request (ApprovalPending) with Location /api/v1/approvals/{id}

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Repeating the request with the same key within 24 hours returns the first answer (header Idempotent-Replayed: true) instead of queuing again; the same key with another request is 422, one still running 409.

patch.description: Sections: general (local_login, stale_hours), network (console_allow, console_block, scim_allow), security (password_policy, four_eyes*, geolocation, fallback_dns), remote_shell, sso (oidc_*, allowed_domain, require_mfa, mfa_acr, role_groups, oidc_client_secret, clear_secret), monitoring (webhook_url, notify_private_networks), branding (company_name, logo_png, remove_logo), operations (ops), retention. Fields left out keep their value. The same guards as the console: no self lockout, local login only off with an OIDC admin, four eyes needs two admins, OIDC changes are checked against the provider. Audited as settings.save.

params.description: The console form fields: minutes (reboot, shutdown), confirm and message (lost, wipe), title and text (message), payload (script), app (app_install, app_remove), username, full_name, password, admin, keep_home (user commands), kind, name, installation (software_remove). true is sent as on; reason (wipe, lost, script: the reason shown to the approving admin when four eyes approval is on).

scope_tags.description: Device scope of a helpdesk or auditor token: only devices with one of these tags are visible and reachable; empty means every device (of the token's tenant). Scoped tokens get no metrics.

tenant_id.description: Tenant of the token; null for a global token. Set from the console's tenant context when the token is created.

action.description: command, user.update, user.add, user.reset, recovery.view or remote_shell

credentials.description: new local credentials of an approved user.add or user.reset, only in the decision's answer

tag.description: one device tag, empty for every device

expires.description: last day it applies, within three years
